entries.title: Keep same-named imports attached to their own library slots
entries.problem: The final binary-model pass keys import slots only by function name and overwrites slots already recorded by the PE parser. Equal names from different libraries, or two explicit imports from one library, end up pointing at the first slot.
entries.change: Match fallback slots by library and function name, and keep the format parser's explicit slot when one is already known.
entries.related_work: #424 preserves already known call-site slots at the engine layer; this corrects the binary model's name-only reassignment across different libraries.
entries.pr_title: Keep same-named imports attached to their own library slots (R3.12)
entries.pr_body:
## Problem

The final binary-model pass keys import slots only by function name and overwrites slots already recorded by the PE parser. Equal names from different libraries, or two explicit imports from one library, end up pointing at the first slot.

## Changes

Match fallback slots by library and function name, and keep the format parser's explicit slot when one is already known.

## Regression coverage

2 regression and control tests in `crates/formats/tests/import_library_slots.rs`.

```sh
cargo test --locked -p craft-anything-formats --test import_library_slots
```

## Validation

Published implementation head: `14b61bb39ae47a4ab1a2b8488fee673a0a02a395`. Existing fork CI is running; final results are being recorded in the contribution manifest. The regression-only version `fbc75b7a38ded5f97b231ae5946d383df8f5410c` reproduced 1 failures with 1 passing controls in isolated remote validation.

## Related work

#424 preserves already known call-site slots at the engine layer; this corrects the binary model's name-only reassignment across different libraries.

## Scope

One R3.12 pending change. Its claim was published separately before implementation.

entries.title: Advance ELF core mapping paths by their original bytes
entries.problem: NT_FILE advances its next filename by the displayed String length. UTF-8 replacement expands byte length, while the 4,096-byte preview cap shortens it, so later mappings acquire bytes from the wrong path.
entries.change: Advance by the original NUL-terminated byte span independently of the retained path preview.
entries.related_work: #906 locates the start of the name table after the full declared mapping count. This corrects each subsequent path's cursor when UTF-8 replacement or preview truncation changes its displayed length.

entries.title: Recover dynamic symbols when retained ELF sections omit the symbol table
entries.problem: Dynamic-symbol recovery is gated on the absence of every section. Files retaining ordinary sections and symbols but lacking a usable dynamic-symbol section lose their PT_DYNAMIC imports and exports.
entries.change: Recover through the existing segment reader when the object parser has no dynamic-symbol entries. Preserve ordinary section/symbol evidence, deduplicate recovered rows and respect the existing global caps.
entries.related_work: #233 explicitly leaves files with some section headers but no .dynsym on the object-only path. This implements that remaining trigger and preserves retained section and ordinary symbol evidence.
entries.pr_title: Recover dynamic symbols when retained ELF sections omit the symbol table (R3.12)

entries.title: Keep ELF symbol versions inside their declared sections
entries.problem: Version definitions, requirements and symbol indices use a reader over the whole ELF file even when section sizes end earlier, so adjacent bytes can be reported as a symbol's version or library.
entries.change: Read each section-backed version carrier through its own declared byte slice, preserving class/endianness and the existing segment-only fallback.
entries.related_work: No matching version_defs/version_needs/.gnu.version correction found in all upstream PR titles and bodies. #1344 concerns dynamic library names bounded by DT_STRSZ, a separate reader.

entries.title: Keep PE import descriptors inside their declared directories
entries.problem: Normal and delay-load descriptors ignore directory sizes, and bound descriptors, forwarder records and names can consume bytes after their directory. Partial metadata is consequently reported as complete imports.
entries.change: Frame all three import metadata readers by their declared directory and contiguous RVA mapping, require complete descriptor/forwarder records, and report truncation. Share the existing resource mapping-extent calculation without changing resource behavior.
entries.related_work: #902 bounds optional headers, #903 resource directories and #1334 header RVA fallback. None bounds the import descriptor directories read by normal_imports, delay_imports and bound_modules.
entries.pr_title: Keep PE import descriptors inside their declared directories (R3.12)
entries.pr_body:
## Problem

Normal and delay-load descriptors ignore directory sizes, and bound descriptors, forwarder records and names can consume bytes after their directory. Partial metadata is consequently reported as complete imports.

## Changes

Frame all three import metadata readers by their declared directory and contiguous RVA mapping, require complete descriptor/forwarder records, and report truncation. Share the existing resource mapping-extent calculation without changing resource behavior.

The existing row-budget test overwrites .facts with 102 complete descriptors but leaves the old three-descriptor directory size. Updated only the declared size to 102 * 20, preserving its 408,000 requested rows and 200,000 output-cap assertion.

entries.title: Reject PE virtual addresses that wrap past the address space
entries.problem: PE entry points, IAT slots and exception function starts add image bases with wrapping arithmetic. Malformed images can produce plausible addresses in unrelated low memory, and PE32 results can leave the 32-bit address space.
entries.change: Check the RVA width, image-base sum and PE32 address width before publishing addresses. Keep import names with unknown slots, omit unrepresentable legacy slot rows, and let PE enrichment own entry-point validation.
entries.related_work: No matching PE image-base address-wrap correction found in all upstream PR titles and bodies. Prior PE changes frame optional headers, resources and header RVA mappings.
entries.pr_title: Reject PE virtual addresses that wrap past the address space (R3.12)

entries.title: Apply PE export limits to aliases and empty function slots
entries.problem: The export row cap is checked before each function, so one function's aliases can overshoot it. Empty function slots do not add rows, allowing a sparse table to bypass the work cap entirely.
entries.change: Bound function slots examined independently of emitted rows and charge aliases against the remaining output budget; report omitted work as truncated.
entries.related_work: No matching PE export alias or sparse-table budget correction found in all upstream PR titles and bodies.

entries.title: Read Mach-O thread entry points from the matching complete CPU state
entries.problem: UNIXTHREAD entry-point decoding ignores each state's declared word count and the image CPU, and reads only the first state. It can publish a PC from incomplete or unrelated state bytes and miss a later supported state.
entries.change: Walk complete count-delimited state records inside the load command, select the supported flavor for the image CPU, and require the complete register layout before reading its PC.
entries.related_work: #899 frames load commands but does not interpret each UNIXTHREAD state count or multiple states. #1278 corrects LC_MAIN segment mapping, not thread states.

entries.title: Bound Mach-O indirect import slots across all sections
entries.problem: The indirect symbol cap resets for every section, so many pointer or stub sections can repeatedly scan the same table and emit an unbounded combined number of import slots.
entries.change: Charge every inspected indirect index, including local and invalid entries, against one image-wide budget and report when unexamined entries remain.
entries.related_work: No matching global indirect-symbol budget correction found in all upstream PR titles and bodies.

entries.title: Reject Objective-C method records shorter than their declared layout
entries.problem: Objective-C method decoding accepts nonzero strides smaller than the absolute or relative layout and publishes methods even when only a record prefix is backed by the section.
entries.change: Require a stride of at least 24 bytes for absolute records or 12 bytes for relative records, and require the complete declared record to be backed before decoding it. Preserve complete extended strides.
entries.related_work: #205 checks method entry address overflow. This rejects too-small absolute/relative record layouts that overlap the next record, while preserving valid extended strides.
